patch_description: The best prior program (score 0.62) was the constant-acceleration Kalman filter with an RTS backward smoother. The current version's added slope-based lead compensation and global Savitzky-Golay polish actually degraded performance (noise_reduction 0.83→0.33, correlation 0.97→0.92) because the lead reintroduced noise and the SG pass was applied everywhere. The new program reverts to the strong Kalman+RTS core and, inspired by the reversal-suppression hysteresis recommendation, adds a *localized* post-stage: it computes the gradient of the smoothed output, flags only short neighborhoods where the gradient sign flips within a few samples while the gradient magnitude is below a fraction of the median gradient magnitude (residual micro-oscillations), and applies a tiny zero-phase order-2 Savitzky-Golay pass only inside those flagged neighborhoods. This directly targets slope_changes and false_reversals without disturbing the well-performing trend structure elsewhere.
